   boundaries per layer times 48 layers at that floor is most of the 871.0 us no matter what protocol moves
   the bits. Fewer boundaries means fusing bodies, and fusion deletes only the flag round trip: the drain
   and the publication survive inside the fused body for every non-owner consumer
   (`docs/PLAN-300TOKS-2026-10-11.md:66-68`).

   grids, every consumer gates the next phase (event counts [256], [24]), and only 6-14 of 38 workers per

   the same worker; 13 of 48 critical moe_up -> moe_down consumers sit on the critical producer's own
   worker (`account.txt:62`). The one measured attempt to move the fetch earlier cost +0.095 ms
   (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:257`).

   lengthens its bodies proportionally (fewer workers stream the same bytes per phase). Fusing the wide
   pairs moves the wait mid-body: the MoE fold is an XCD-local all-to-all of 24 producers (event E_8,
   counts [24]), so a fused moe_up+moe_down task still polls the same flag between its halves.

211.claim: **Compute: no pair of phases is independent.** The decoder layer is a serial chain, qkv -> prep -> attn -> reduce -> o_proj -> router -> topk -> moe_up -> moe_down -> next layer's qkv (the layer order of `account.txt:82-143`), and every consecutive pair carries a measured dependency edge in the trace (`account.txt:62-79`). The brief's example needs a correction here: layer N's `attn` and `reduce` are indeed dependent, but layer N's `moe_down` and layer N+1's `qkv` are **not** independent either — the trace measures 47 such edges and 190.2 us of gaps on them (`account.txt:63,65`) [M], because qkv_{N+1} reads the residual stream that moe_down_N produces (the input/residual norm is folded into qkv). 224.claim:
1. **The idle is a symptom, not a resource.** A worker idles because its next task's inputs do not exist yet. Section 3 shows there is no independent compute to give it: every consecutive phase pair is dependency-linked in the trace, including the pair the brief calls independent (moe_down_N -> qkv_{N+1}, 47 measured edges, `account.txt:63,65`). The only thing that can move into the idle time is weight traffic, and weight traffic's value is bounded by the cache-rate delta, measured at +9% at layer size and negative at window size (`overlap.log:3-8`).
2. **Filling the idle ports has a measured price on the work that matters.** The fold benchmark on this GPU: the latency chain's round trip went 1.52 -> 3.08 us when a background stream filled the idle bandwidth (`overlap.log:15-16`). The latency phases carry 396.4 us of exposed hops [E]; a slowdown there is paid on the critical path, while the prefetch benefit is bounded at 63-121 us [E]. The mechanism can be net negative even when it works.
3. **It has been tried, twice, on this GPU.** Fleet's idle-worker prefetch of routing-independent weights into the Infinity Cache: no gain, 4.84 vs 4.80 ms, with the reason recorded — the per-CU streaming rate (~30 GB/s) caps what idle workers can pull, and the phases that would benefit are latency-bound, not byte-bound (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:72`). Cross-task prefetch across the event wait: 4% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:30`). And ETX's own touch hook is already the within-phase version of this mechanism — waves 1-15 pull the task's first weights into L2 during the dependency wait (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:283-290`) — and its value after `ETX_VL_COH` was never isolated (`docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27`).
4. **Caching cannot shorten the latency that dominates.** The loaded round trip is level-independent (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`), so residency touches only bandwidth exposure, which section 4 bounds at 2.7% of the span in the most favourable case.
